result.title: Quantiles, Not Points: Streaming Quantile Matching for Ordinal-Aware LLM-as-a-Judge Calibration
result.summary: LLM-as-a-judge scores are often distributionally shifted from human ratings on any given evaluation task, and post-hoc calibration (mapping LLM to human scores in a small labeled anchor set) has become a popular method to correct for this shift. In this paper we derive the calibration from two positions: that LLMaJ scores are ordinal ratings drawn from a distribution rather than isolated points. We present streaming quantile matching (SQM), a version of a classical method not previously bench marked for LLMaJ calibration, which is built on the two positions by computing the optimal-transport map between the LLM and human score distributions. We develop an evaluation framework and within it we show that unlike point-wise calibrations, SQM respects the ordinality of the human anchor set and achieves the best distributional fidelity and the top overall rank across models and data. We also show that in general, post-hoc calibration narrows the raw error gap between smaller and larger judge models, which opens the possibility of more efficient LLM judges.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 LLM-as-a-judge 的评分视为来自分布的序数评级而非孤立点，提出 streaming quantile matching（SQM），用最优传输映射对齐 LLM 与人类评分分布，并在自建评测框架中与逐点校准方法比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按分布而非逐点比较」的思路可能启发 latent 状态或推理轨迹相似度的度量方式（如用分布级对齐替代单点距离），但与原论文的视觉推理机制无直接关系，可供核查。
